name: Thread-Safe LLD: Locking, Condition Variables & In-Memory Pub-Sub Queues
tagline: Balancing correctness and throughput using fine-grained per-entity locks, Condition signaling, and canonical lock ordering.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of thread-safe low-level design—from why coarse global mutexes stall throughput to how per-topic locks, Condition.await(), and lock ordering prevent deadlocks.

spark.summary: Thread-safe Low-Level Design balances correctness and throughput using fine-grained per-entity locks (per-seat, per-topic, per-floor), Condition/BlockingQueue signaling, and optimistic versioning rather than coarse global mutexes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Lock at the smallest independent boundary (e.g., per-topic or per-seat) and always acquire multiple locks in a canonical global order to prevent deadlocks.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Thread-safe Low-Level Design structures shared in-memory state—bounded blocking queues, pub-sub topics, and seat reservation maps—so concurrent threads never corrupt invariants or busy-wait CPU cores.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Bounded Queue Producer/Consumer Thread States (HOLDING LOCK -> AWAITING COND -> SIGNALED); Canonical Lock Ordering (min(id) -> max(id)) (Thread 1 (B, A) -> Lock(Seat A) -> Lock(Seat B) -> Thread 2 (A, B)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose the simplest synchronization boundary that meets your contention profile. In an in-memory pub-sub broker, publishers append to the topic ring buffer under the per-topic lock, then **dispatch to subscribers outside the lock** (or via per-subscriber.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Practice implementing bounded queues, pub-sub brokers, and deadlock-free booking systems.

learningJourney.title: What is Thread-Safe Concurrency LLD
learningJourney.explanation:
Thread-safe Low-Level Design structures shared in-memory state—bounded blocking queues, pub-sub topics, and seat reservation maps—so concurrent threads never corrupt invariants or busy-wait CPU cores.

Three primitives form the core toolkit: **fine-grained per-entity locks** (`ReentrantLock` per topic or seat), **Condition variables** (`notFull` / `notEmpty`) so waiting threads sleep without spinning, and **canonical lock ordering** to prevent AB-BA deadlocks.

learningJourney.title: Why coarse locks and slow callbacks break concurrent LLD
learningJourney.explanation:
A single `synchronized` method on a broker or booking service serializes unrelated topics and seats, collapsing multi-core throughput. Conversely, naive fine-grained locking introduces two classic bugs:
- **AB-BA Deadlocks**: Thread 1 locks Seat A then Seat B while Thread 2 locks Seat B then Seat A.
- **Lock-Held Callback Stalls**: Invoking slow external subscriber callbacks while holding the topic lock blocks all publishers.

sectionDiagram.title: Canonical Lock Ordering (min(id) -> max(id))
sectionDiagram.summary: Sorting lock IDs globally guarantees a strict acquisition DAG, making circular wait mathematically impossible.

benefits: Sub-millisecond per-seat locking with TTL expiry sweeps.
costs: Cannot coordinate across multiple JVM/service instances.

learningJourney.title: Implementing a Bounded Blocking Queue with Condition Variables
learningJourney.explanation: Separate `notFull` and `notEmpty` `Condition` queues on a `ReentrantLock`, always guard `await()` with a `while` loop, and always release the lock in a `finally` block.

learningJourney.explanation: Choose the simplest synchronization boundary that meets your contention profile.

benefits: Trivial to reason about; zero multi-lock deadlock risk.
costs: Serializes unrelated topics/seats; poor multi-core scaling.

benefits: High parallel throughput across independent entities.
costs: Requires strict canonical lock ordering on multi-entity operations.

benefits: Zero OS mutex context switches; ultra-low tail latency.
costs: Complex memory-ordering invariants and harder debugging.

learningJourney.title: Snapshot-and-Dispatch Pub-Sub Pattern
learningJourney.explanation: In an in-memory pub-sub broker, publishers append to the topic ring buffer under the per-topic lock, then **dispatch to subscribers outside the lock** (or via per-subscriber worker threads with offset pointers) so slow consumers never stall publishers.

ideas.description: Each subscriber maintains an atomic offset into the topic's immutable message array, allowing independent consumption speeds.

ideas.title: TryLock with Timeout
ideas.description: For latency-sensitive APIs, pair canonical ordering with `tryLock(50, MILLISECONDS)` to fail fast instead of piling up threads.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why must a consumer thread check its wait condition in a `while` loop rather than an `if` statement around `Condition.await()`?

options.text: Condition.await() throws an exception if called inside an if block
options.feedback: The compiler allows if, but it is unsafe at runtime.

options.text: Spurious wakeups or another competing consumer waking first can leave the queue empty again before this thread re-acquires the lock
options.feedback: Correct: Mesa-style condition variables do not guarantee the predicate still holds when a thread resumes, so re-checking in a while loop is mandatory.

options.text: A while loop prevents the thread from releasing the ReentrantLock
options.feedback: Condition.await() always atomically releases the lock while sleeping.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** Thread-safe Low-Level Design structures shared in-memory state—bounded blocking queues, pub-sub topics, and seat reservation maps—so concurrent threads never corrupt invariants or busy-wait CPU cores.

**How It Flows:** Think of Thread-Safe LLD: Locking, Condition Variables & In-Memory Pub-Sub Queues as a clear step-by-step chain: HOLDING LOCK -> AWAITING COND -> SIGNALED -> Thread 1 (B, A) -> Lock(Seat A).

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Lock at the smallest independent boundary (e.g., per-topic or per-seat) and always acquire multiple locks in a canonical global order to prevent deadlocks.
